title: Simulating Natural Selection
subject: Biology
beats: Previous sims used fixed odds; now selection must come from traits meeting an environment
The world: food appears daily; 0 food dies, 1 survives, 2 replicates
Watch a few generations first: population grows to carrying capacity of about 95
Turn on one trait, speed, with a cost: double speed, double energy per distance
What would you predict? Lists four plausible outcomes
Speed wins here, or at least the starting value was too slow
First example of natural selection: random variation plus selection raises average speed
Populations evolve, not individuals, despite Pokemon
Population shrinks as speed rises: selection isn't for the good of the species
Add size: eat creatures 20% smaller, but energy cost scales with size cubed
Admits the cost function is a choice; size cubed times speed squared, like kinetic energy
Add sense: see food or threats from farther, at a cost
Rewind and vary all three; a 3D scatter plots each creature
Average speed differs from before: other creatures are part of the environment
He expected strong selection for sense; it didn't happen
Drop food to 10 a day: he says he doesn't know what will happen
Sudden drop kills everyone; rewind and lower food gradually
Big loses, sense and speed win; his efficiency guess was wrong again
Environment matters; evolution is not a march toward higher creatures
Quick recap; next videos explore counterintuitive traits

meta.notation_note: Only one formula (size cubed x speed squared), spoken and immediately tied to kinetic energy. The main new interface is a 3D trait scatter at 5:53.
meta.misconception: yes: 3:27 (individuals evolve), 6:49 and 8:24 (the presenter's own predictions fail), 8:42 (evolution as a march of progress)
meta.brute_force: yes 1:05: watches the population run with no mutations before adding traits one at a time
meta.examples: 4 runs: no mutation, speed only, three traits, food scarcity
meta.examples_grow: grows in complexity: one trait, three traits, a changing environment
quote: It. Just does what it does.
